title: External agent tooling source-evidence intake and disposition
trigger: A new tool, framework, plugin, provider, protocol, database, skill suite, or architecture is proposed for AgentSwitchboard evaluation or adoption.

steps.action: Preserve the literal source claim and aliases without upgrading it to fact.
steps.output: catalog candidate with reported or unresolved evidence state

steps.action: Classify kind, category, mention class, and proposed disposition.
Search current AgentSwitchboard capability, execution-adapter, prompt, harness, validator, workflow, and documentation owners before proposing new ownership.
Before adoption, verify official upstream identity plus pinned version/commit, supported OS, install scope, expected files, and rollback path.
steps.output: upstream verification evidence or unresolved blocker

steps.action: Determine permissions, subprocess/filesystem/network behavior, provider credentials, persistence, updates, telemetry, and whether local/private claims are actually proven.

Keep catalog capabilityState unknown and runtime/trust/privacy proof unproved. Route any live capability or execution claim to CAPABILITIES.md or the owning runtime contract; never promote from catalog presence.
steps.output: source-only proof state or explicit external proof owner

steps.action: Choose existing-reference, evaluate, compatibility, supporting, comparison, watchlist, or open a separately scoped implementation/evaluation sprint.
Run leaf catalog validators, current operational harness validation, and git diff --check.

stopConditions: required official source cannot be verified
installation or execution would exceed current sprint authority
another canonical repo surface already owns the integration
a catalog entry attempts to promote itself above unknown/unproved capability, runtime, trust, or privacy state
outputs: updated tracked registry when source evidence changes
external-agent-tooling-evaluation.json for a separately authorized bounded evaluation
separate implementation sprint when adoption is approved
proofCeiling: Source evidence intake, classification, overlap analysis, and versioned upstream metadata when actually collected; no installation, capability, trust, privacy, provider, or runtime proof.
